headline: Will I love again?
note: SELF-FRAME. The reading is about HER OWN FUTURE. Bans, and why each one is here: (1) NO MAN. Nobody exists in this read yet, so no he/him/his anywhere, and the dream figure is never given a person's motive. A lander with no man in it that borrows decode-him habits invents one, and a soulmate search turns into reunion copy she never asked for. (2) The hopeful YES IS ALLOWED and is affirmed flat in cut 3 — that is the half the ad already sold her, and hedging it is what makes a read feel like a con. (3) WITHHOLD ONLY THE SPECIFICS: no name, no date, no timeframe or duration (a length is not a date and is banned anyway — 'not much longer' was the soulmate age-band gap), no exactly-who, no WHERE (the soulmate-where gap: the standing clause said name/date/who and forgot place). A date is the only claim she can check, and a failed one is a refund. (4) NOT A DEATH. She is heartbroken, not bereaved — no mediumship, no contact, no language that reads as loss of life. (5) NO BLAME. Never pathologise her, never make the break her fault, never a quantified probability. (6) CUT 6 USES THE CLOSED EVIDENCE SET ONLY — her question plus what cuts 1-5 already established from the dream. No invented count, habit, event or life pattern, and it never certifies that she was right. (7) THE DREAM MEANS WHAT IT MEANS. All three panels are control-loss dreams — pursued, unsupported, coming apart — which is what heartbreak feels like, so the read answers her yes IN SPITE of the picture and never strains to make the dream itself be about love. The dream is a picture she is looking at: it gets no intent and no motion of its own, and SHE stays the subject from cut 3 on.

voc.why: inherits the shipped palm love-again finding; the dream panels are survey-sourced, not VOC-sourced

a: You're running, and you never turn round to see what's behind you. Your legs won't move the way they should.
You're asking if you'll love again. Legs that won't carry you mean you've been trying to get away from something and getting nowhere.
You're not being hunted. What's behind you is the part of you that still wants love, and yes, you'll love again.
The dream shows you running. It doesn't show you stopping, or what you'd do if you turned round.
You still want love, and none has come. Every time this dream comes back, you spend it moving further away.
Keeping ahead of what you want takes everything you've got. No wonder your legs give out.
Let me look closer at what set you running in the first place…
b: You're falling. There's nothing underneath you, and you wake with that jolt just before you land.
You're asking whether you'll love again. Falling with nothing under you is what it feels like to be held by no one.
You've already made that fall once, and you're still here. Your heart still opens, dear, and love is finding its way back.
The dream stops before you land. Nothing in it ever shows you safe on the ground.
You came through that fall, and you still wake up braced. Your body's still getting ready for a landing that never comes.
You're not asking whether you can love again. You're asking whether anyone will be there to catch you this time.
Let me see what keeps you braced when the fall's already behind you…
c: Your teeth have gone loose. You put your hand up and they come away, one after another, into your palm.
You're asking if love will come again. Teeth coming out like that is the fear of falling apart where people can see it.
Nothing that mattered was taken. What came away was what you showed people — you can still love, and you will.
The dream ends with them in your palm. You don't see yourself afterwards, and nobody else does either.
You can see exactly what came away, down to the last one. The part that's still yours doesn't show up anywhere.
You'd rather not be looked at too closely just now, and you still want to be loved, dear. Those two pull opposite ways.
Now let me look at what you think you lost with them…
